claim.pdf_says: 14.7.5   SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition   [same clause depth as 14.7.1 General, 14.7.4 ROUNDED phrase, 14.7.6 CORRESPONDING phrase]
claim.markdown_says: ### 14.7.5 SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24682)
claim.why_it_matters: Every sibling clause in the run is transcribed at '##' - 14.7 (24595), 14.7.1 (24598), 14.7.2 (24610), 14.7.3 (24615), 14.7.4 (24620), 14.7.6 (24754), 14.7.7 (24790), 14.7.8 (24846), 14.7.9 (24874). 14.7.5 alone is at '###', so it nests under 14.7.4 in any TOC or heading-depth walk instead of being its own clause, which misplaces the SIZE ERROR clause relative to ROUNDED.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED as a structural transcription error, though the 'missing-heading' label is a misnomer - the heading is present, it is at the wrong depth.

What I independently checked:

1. PDF page 591 (rendered at 300 dpi, printed page 561). The heading reads exactly '14.7.5   SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition', bold, flush left, with the two-em gap between number and title that ISO uses for every clause heading. The markdown transcribes that text verbatim - no word is missing, nothing is reflowed onto an adjacent line, and the body text that follows ('The size error condition may occur as a result of the execution of an ADD, COMPUTE, DIVIDE, GENERATE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statement...') plus both em-dash bullets match the PDF word for word. So the 'missing text' failure mode does not apply and the claim's kind label is wrong.

2. The real defect is the heading LEVEL. I rendered page 590 to see how ISO distinguishes depths: 14.7.2 'At end condition', 14.7.3 'Invalid key condition' and 14.7.4 'ROUNDED phrase' sit alongside 14.7.4.1 'General', 14.7.4.2 'General format', 14.7.4.3 'General rules', and ISO renders all six in the identical bold face and point size. Typography carries NO depth information in this document - depth is carried entirely by the dotted number. '14.7.5' has three components, exactly like '14.7.4'; the subclauses of 14.7.4 are numbered 14.7.4.1/.2/.3. Therefore 14.7.5 is unambiguously a SIBLING of 14.7.4 in the PDF and cannot be a child of it. This is decidable from the printed glyphs alone and is not a matter of interpretation.

3. The markdown assigns 14.7.5 the same '###' level it assigns to 14.7.4.1, 14.7.4.2 and 14.7.4.3, so a heading-depth walk parents SIZE ERROR under ROUNDED phrase. I verified the surrounding run directly (grep '^#{1,4} 14\.7(\.\d+)*'): 24598 '## 14.7', 24601 '## 14.7.1', 24613 '## 14.7.2', 24618 '## 14.7.3', 24623 '## 14.7.4', 24626 '### 14.7.4.1', 24633 '### 14.7.4.2', 24649 '### 14.7.4.3', 24685 '### 14.7.5', 24757 '## 14.7.6', 24793 '## 14.7.7', 24849 '## 14.7.8', 24877 '## 14.7.9', 24880 '### 14.7.9.1', 24885 '### 14.7.9.2', 24896 '### 14.7.9.3'. The claim's assertion that every sibling in the run is at '##' and that 14.7.5 alone is at '###' is exactly right. Within this run the convention (three-component = '##', four-component = '###') is otherwise perfectly consistent, including the parallel 14.7.9/14.7.9.x pair, so 14.7.5 is a genuine outlier and not an artifact of an absent convention.

4. I did try to refute on the 'it is only formatting' ground and rejected that. In a transcription of a numbered standard the heading level is the only machine-readable encoding of clause hierarchy; it is content, not presentation. Under the current markdown a TOC build or a section-extraction walk reports SIZE ERROR as part of the ROUNDED phrase clause, which is substantively false - SIZE ERROR is an independent common phrase, and 14.7.5's own body cross-references EC-SIZE and TURN, nothing about rounding. That said, no rule text, cross-reference or citation string is altered, and the '14.7.5' number itself is correct in the markdown, so a reader or a citation-by-number lookup is unaffected. 'cosmetic' severity is the right call.

Inaccuracies in the claim that do not change the verdict: (a) the kind should be 'wrong-heading-level', not 'missing-heading'; (b) every line number cited is low by 3 - 14.7.5 is at line 24685, not 24682, and likewise 14.7 is at 24598 not 24595, 14.7.1 at 24601 not 24598, 14.7.2 at 24613 not 24610, 14.7.3 at 24618 not 24615, 14.7.4 at 24623 not 24620, 14.7.6 at 24757 not 24754, 14.7.7 at 24793 not 24790, 14.7.8 at 24849 not 24846, 14.7.9 at 24877 not 24874. The uniform -3 offset suggests the claim was generated against a slightly earlier snapshot of specs/ISO_COBOL.md; the quoted heading TEXT and the quoted '###'/'##' levels are all correct as of the current file.

Out-of-scope observation found while checking the convention, flagged for a separate work item, not part of this verdict: the 14.6.13 region of the markdown appears to contain a duplicated block - '## 14.6.13 Exception condition handling' occurs at both 24101 and 24142, and '14.6.13.1.1 General' occurs at 24107 as '##' and again at 24148 as '####'. That is a different page and a materially larger problem than a single heading level.
verdict.corrected_description: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24685 transcribes clause 14.7.5 as '### 14.7.5 SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition' when it should be '## 14.7.5 ...'. The heading text is present and byte-for-byte faithful to the PDF (page 591 / printed 561); nothing is missing. The defect is the heading DEPTH: ISO renders all clause headings in one typeface, so depth is carried by the dotted number alone, and '14.7.5' is a three-component number and hence a sibling of '14.7.4 ROUNDED phrase', whose own subclauses are numbered 14.7.4.1/.2/.3. Because the markdown gives 14.7.5 the same '###' level as 14.7.4.1-.3, any TOC build or heading-depth walk parents the SIZE ERROR clause under the ROUNDED phrase clause. All nine siblings in the run are correctly at '##' (14.7 at 24598, 14.7.1 at 24601, 14.7.2 at 24613, 14.7.3 at 24618, 14.7.4 at 24623, 14.7.6 at 24757, 14.7.7 at 24793, 14.7.8 at 24849, 14.7.9 at 24877), so 14.7.5 is the sole outlier. Fix: change '###' to '##' on line 24685. Reclassify kind from 'missing-heading' to 'wrong-heading-level'; severity 'cosmetic' is correct since no rule text or citable clause number is altered.
